reason: The motor is the only available action and should provide the drive for both attractions.
expectation: I expect to mount the motor on the whale; it will probably still need connections and speed reduction.

effect: The motor is mounted; it still needs connections to the attractions.
reaction: The result is straightforward, with no detail yet about the drive.
reason: The coupler is the only offered combination and should connect the motor to a crank.
expectation: I expect it to connect the motor to the dragon's crank, though the exact arrangement is uncertain.

effect: The dragon is now motor-driven; the star theatre still needs its drive.
reaction: The connection makes sense, though the result gives no mechanical detail.
reason: The reducing belt drive is the only offered combination and should connect the remaining attraction at a different speed.
expectation: I expect the belt drive to connect the star theatre and slow its rotation, though the exact speed relationship is unclear.

effect: The belt drive slows the star wheel relative to the dragon using different-sized pulleys.
reaction: The contrast between drifting stars and brisk waves makes the pulley reduction clear.
reason: The cover is the only offered combination and should shield the moving drive.
expectation: I expect a transparent guard to cover the belt and pulleys while leaving them visible.

effect: The drive is now guarded; it still needs to be switched on.
reaction: The cover is a sensible safety step, though the result gives no further detail.
reason: The switch key is the only offered combination and should let me test the attractions.
expectation: I expect the motor to run the dragon and star wheel at their different speeds.

effect: The test confirms that both attractions run together, and the slipping clutch provides protection if the dragon is held still. Everything is switched off for the later lift test.
reaction: Seeing the dragon wave while the stars crawl is a satisfying payoff; the clutch was a useful extra detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the reducing belt drive was most worthwhile: the different-sized pulleys explain why the stars move slowly while the dragon waves briskly.

leastWorthwhile.text: Mounting the motor and fitting the coupler felt rather routine; their results gave little mechanical detail.

surprise.text: The clutch slipping gently when the dragon is held still was an unexpected protective feature.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, although the coupler's exact arrangement was not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see the assembled whale take its lifting test; this chapter made the two attractions work together but left the flight ahead.
